entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to FIR No. 67/2024 registered at Police Station - Maharajpura, District - Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363, 366, 376 (3), 376(D) of IPC and Section 5G/6 of POCSO Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant - accused argued that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.

Allegedly, the prosecutrix got missing on 24.1.2024 and was recovered on 22.2.2024,
however, in her statement recorded just after recovery under Section 164 Cr.P.C. dated 22.2.2024,
she has not supported the case of the prosecution and stated that she wanted to marry Chhotu, and therefore, left her house.
It is further argued that after investigation, charge-sheet has already been filed.
Prosecutrix as well as her parents have been examined as PW-1 to PW-3, however, they have not supported the case of the prosecution and turned hostile.
Even they stated that age of the prosecutrix is 19 years.
Under these circumstances, entire prosecution story becomes doubtful.
Further argument is that applicant is in 2 MCRC-24798-2024 custody since 11.4.2024.
Custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required anymore.
Applicant is the permanent resident of District Gwalior (M.P.).
Since evidence of the prosecutrix and her parents have already been recorded, therefore, the question of influencing them does not arise.
Hence, prayed for grant of bail to the applicant.
On the other hand, learned State counsel opposed the bail application and prayed for rejection of the same.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) along with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/Committal Court.
Learned State counsel is directed to send an e-copy of this order to the Station House Officer of the concerned Police Station for information and necessary action.
E- copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance, if possible, by the office of this Court.
Certified copy as per rules.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE AKS Surendra Singh Rana vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44326953/
